content.title: About
content.content: A wheat muffin is a small baked good made from wheat flour, eggs, milk, sugar, and leavening agents. It has a soft, slightly moist crumb and a mildly sweet flavor, often enhanced with berries, nuts, or chocolate chips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Muffins originated in the United States in the early 19th century as a quick way to use leftover batter.
Wheat flour in muffins provides a good source of complex carbohydrates and fiber.
There are more than 30 flavor variations: blueberry, banana, chocolate, carrot, and others.
Muffins are commonly served for breakfast or as a snack in cafés.
Traditionally muffins are baked in paper liners, which makes them easy to transport.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The carbohydrates supply quick energy, making muffins a convenient snack.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour is rich in thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Helps digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Eggs and milk add both animal and plant protein, important for tissue repair.

items.title: Antioxidants (when berries are added)
items.content: Blueberries, raspberries, or other berries provide antioxidants that protect cells.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet muffins can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat flour contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Egg and dairy allergy
items.content: The recipe includes eggs and milk, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Muffins are relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Muffins can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, sliced and spread with cream cheese, nut butter, or jam. They are often paired with tea or coffee and can be served to children in small portions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or freeze in a bag for up to 3 months. Reheat in the oven or microwave before eating.
